name: Dialog etre Arzur ha Guynglaff
text: The Dialog etre Arzur ha Guynglaff is a verse piece in Middle Breton. Its full title names its two speakers. Arthur leads the exchange as a ruler of the Bretons. Guynglaff answers him across the whole talk. The piece works in the manner of a prophecy. It belongs to a set of Middle Breton sacred verse. That set includes later religious poems of the region. Within this body the dialogue ranks as the leading work. Its standing gives it a special worth. It gives rare proof of prophecy verse in Breton. The piece holds a central place in the Breton record.

okr.objective: Record the Middle Breton prophetic dialogue between Arthur and Guynglaff as the leading verse in its group.
key_results: Capture the full title and its English sense.
Name Arthur as ruler of the Bretons and his companion Guynglaff.
Rate the piece above the other works in the same group.
okr.evidence: The source calls the dialogue a prophetic verse exchange between Arthur, ruler of the Bretons, and Guynglaff. It ranks the work first among the pieces in the set. Koch 2006 includes the dialogue in the Breton literature entry.

sources: Koch 2006, s.v. "Dialog etre Arzur ha Guynglaff"
